This pull request aims to improve Mixxx's beat and tempo analysis and add
downbeat markers to constant-tempo tracks using the Beat This! algorithm.

The motivation was simple: incorrect beatgrids and BPM values—often half or
two-thirds of the actual tempo—and missing downbeat markers required too much
manual correction.

My goal is to match or eventually exceed the analysis quality of commercial DJ
software such as Traktor, Serato and rekordbox. To guide development, I tested
76 particularly challenging tracks from this playlist: **[playlist link to be
added]**. Many are vinyl rips; ordinary digital releases have generally caused
fewer problems in my testing. Two rounds of refinement addressed the reported
failures, resolving around ten especially difficult cases in my checks.

## Features

- **Local Beat This! integration:** neural beat and downbeat detection using
  CPU inference. Audio stays on your computer.
- **Auto, Constant and Variable:** automatic grid selection, conservative
  drift checks and explicit global or per-track overrides.
- **Custom Models:** independently assign Beat This! or Queen Mary to Constant
  and Variable; Auto uses these assignments.
- **Audio-based grid refinement:** corrections for half-/two-thirds-tempo
  errors, misplaced beat lines and false variable detections when supported
  by the audio, including safeguards against late bass-crest alignment.
- **Downbeat markers:** stored, wider waveform markers for constant and
  variable grids; optional native Queen Mary 4/4 downbeat estimation.
- **Persistent analysis workers:** reuse the loaded Python model across tracks,
  with progress reporting, cancellation, result validation and crash recovery.
- **User-local Linux installer:** isolated Python/model setup, automatic paths,
  compile-only or desktop installation, and 25%/50%/75% compile RAM budgets.
- **Benchmark tools:** strict musical BPM, beat/downbeat timing, grid stability,
  correction effort and performance metrics, with development/holdout separation.

## Validation and status

The automated suite includes 21 real-track development regressions, separately
from my 76-track evaluation. The latest validation passed 1,351 C++ and 62 Python
tests. Existing BPM locks and reanalysis preferences remain respected.

Commercial parity and universally perfect grids are goals, not established
results. A representative, independently annotated holdout and controlled
comparisons with commercial software are still needed.

For Linux setup, use `python3 tools/install-linux.py` from this branch. See
[LINUX_INSTALL.md](LINUX_INSTALL.md) for installation details and
[BEAT_BENCHMARK.md](BEAT_BENCHMARK.md) for the evaluation methodology.
